newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea plans Korea First Bank loan.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea plans Korea First Bank loan.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea plans to extend special loans to Korea First Bank, but only if Korea First submits an agreement in writing by its labour union on a huge workforce cut, newspaper reports said on Thursday.
Friday editions of leading newspapers received late on Thursday quoted Bank of Korea governor Lee Kyung-shick as saying Korea First's self-rescue plans "should precede a special loan".

"(Korea First Bank ) has to submit to the Bank of Korea strong self-rescue plans including the labour union's agreement letting the bank's management cut the workforce," the Dong-A Ilbo quoted Lee as saying.
Korea First has been hit by a string of defaults by some of its major client companies.
Korea First is the largest creditor to the stricken Hanbo Group and the largest commercial bank among creditors to the troubled Kia Group.

The Hanbo Group's flagship Hanbo Steel Co, the country's second-largest steelmaker, was declared insolvent in January while the Kia Group has been put under the two-month protection by banks from defaulting on debt payments.
The Chosun Ilbo said the loan would carry an interest rate of three percent per annum, much lower than the central bank's rediscounting rate of seven percent.
Lee was quoted as saying the central bank planned to extend the loan "in the near future", but no time table was given by any of the newspaper reports.
The Bank of Korea said on Wednesday it had supplied $1 billion to seven commercial banks to ease dollar shortages at the local banking system.
